before.existing_compacted_memory: Alice (Nodes 20, 25) aims to settle Node 9 (3:1 port) then Node 32. Hand: 1 Wood, 1 Wheat, 1 Sheep + Monopoly card. Target resources: Brick and Wood. Robber moved from Hex 5 (Brick 6) to Hex 7 (Wheat 8), now blocking Alice and Charlie. Bob (Nodes 12, 43) is the primary antagonist and just rolled a 7 to move the robber. Charlie (Nodes 41, 14) remains a loyal ally; he recently bought a dev card and is hoarding Wood for his own settlement near Node 7. Charlie and Alice have a mutual pact against Bob and have prioritized 1:1 trading, though Charlie currently refuses to trade Wood. Alice holds a Monopoly card for a potential strategic strike.

Bob stole from Charlie after moving the robber to Hex 7 (Wheat 8). Charlie likely has wood since Bob mentioned wood rolls. I still have my Monopoly card; I should wait for a high-yield roll to use it.
Rejected Bob's 1:1 Sheep for Wood. I need to keep my Wood for Node 9 and I'm not helping Bob after he blocked my Wheat 8.

recent_notes_kept_verbatim.note: Charlie bought a development card after failing to find brick. He has 3 wood left. Bob is still the main target. Hand: 1W, 1Wh, 2S.

relevant_chat.message: Spoken like a true 'community' leader, Bob. Always looking for ways to share the burden.
Balance the scales? You're just hitting the only person who hasn't tried to backstab me yet, Bob.
Alice, you're always talking about community. How about a little neighborly swap? I'll give you some prime wool for a bit of that wood you've got lying around.
You just put a 'guest' in my wheat field, Bob, and now you want my wood? I think I'll pass. I'm sure you can find someone else to 'balance the scales' with.
Much better. That field was getting a bit crowded anyway.
Alice, I'm looking for a bit of brick to finish my path. Would you be interested in some wood in exchange?
I'd love to help out, Charlie, but I don't have any brick either. Bob seems to be the only one sitting on the clay lately.
Well, at least the woods are providing. Since nobody has any clay to spare, I'll just hold onto these logs for now. Your turn, Alice.
I figured you’d be eager to move that, Bob. Just don't get too comfortable with wherever you're putting it.
Sorry Charlie, but you've been a bit too successful with those wood rolls lately. I need to balance the scales a little.
Balance the scales? You're just mad about that blocked brick, Bob. Don't worry, I'll remember the favor.

Look, Charlie, I know the robber is a bit of a nuisance, but I'm looking to move things along. You've got bricks, I've got plenty of wheat for those cities you'll want later. Three wheat for one brick? It's a steal.
I don't have any brick for you, Bob. Maybe if you hadn't just robbed me, I'd be more inclined to help you find some.
Charlie, I know you said you were out of brick, but surely three bags of wheat is enough to make you check your pockets again? It's a massive overpay, but I'm feeling generous after that seven.
I'm not hiding anything, Bob. I still have zero brick. Checking my pockets won't change the fact that you're asking for something I don't have.
Well, if the bricks are as scarce as the hospitality around here, I suppose I'll just have to wait. Good luck with the next roll, everyone.

You know, Bob, you talk a lot about 'balancing scales,' but I think it's time we actually leveled the field. That Wheat 8 was doing just fine without your 'guest.' Let's see how you like it when your bricks go missing for a change.
A bit dramatic for a simple knight, don't you think, Charlie? I'm just a humble merchant trying to keep the wheat flowing.
Alright, let's see what the dice have to say about this 'balance' you keep talking about, Bob.
Well, looks like the bricks are as dry as the desert right now. I'll just have to see what else I can find in the deck.
